items.title: Two Practices That Understate the Mental Health Risks Associated With Adolescent Social-Media Use.
items.venue: Perspectives on psychological science : a journal of the Association for Psychological Science
items.summary: Why do researchers analyzing the same body of evidence reach different conclusions about whether social-media use poses risks to adolescent mental health? We offer a partial explanation: Two common practices can lead researchers to underestimate harm and reach divergent conclusions. First, studies often do not account for risk elevations, relying instead only on correlation coefficients, which are more prone to misinterpretation.
